    if np.any(valid):
        # Normalize by bin size to avoid bias toward larger bins
        normalized_remaining = remaining[valid] / bins[valid]
        # Higher priority for smaller remaining space (closer to full)
        pri[valid] = 1.0 - normalized_remaining

def priority(item: float, bins: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Returns priority with which we want to add item to each bin.
    Args:
        item: Size of item to be added to the bin.
        bins: Array of capacities for each bin.
    Return:
        Array of same size as bins with priority score of each bin.
    """
    remaining = bins - item
    valid = remaining >= 0
    pri = np.zeros_like(bins, dtype=float)
    if np.any(valid):
        current_utilization = (bins[valid] - remaining[valid]) / bins[valid]
        new_utilization = (bins[valid] - remaining[valid] + item) / bins[valid]
        improvement = new_utilization - current_utilization
        # Logarithmic scaling to emphasize improvements in less full bins
        pri[valid] = np.log1p(improvement * bins[valid])
    return pri

    Args:

        bins: Array of capacities for each bin.

        Array of same size as bins with priority score of each bin.
    """
    remaining = bins - item
    valid = remaining >= 0
    pri = np.zeros_like(bins, dtype=float)
    if np.any(valid):
        target_remaining = bins[valid] * 0.3  # Target: 30% of bin size remaining
        deviation = np.abs(remaining[valid] - target_remaining)
        # Normalize deviation by bin size for fairness
        normalized_deviation = deviation / bins[valid]
        # Higher priority for smaller deviation (closer to target)
        pri[valid] = 1.0 / (1.0 + normalized_deviation)
    return pri

def priority(item: float, bins: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    remaining = bins - item
    valid = remaining >= 0
    pri = np.zeros_like(bins, dtype=float)
    if np.any(valid):
        # Check for exact divisor relationship (with tolerance for floating point)
        tolerance = 1e-12
        divisible = np.abs(remaining[valid] % item) <= tolerance
        # Assign higher base priority to bins where item divides remaining capacity
        pri[valid] = np.where(divisible, 2.0, 1.0)
        # Add tie-breaker based on remaining capacity (larger remaining gets slight boost)
        pri[valid] += remaining[valid] / (bins[valid] + 1e-12) * 0.1
    return pri

def priority(item: float, bins: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    remaining = bins - np.clip(bins, 0, item)
    
    # Bins that cannot fit the item get very low priority (negative infinity)
    can_fit = remaining >= item
    priorities = np.full_like(bins, -np.inf)
    
    # For bins that can fit the item, prioritize based on remaining capacity after adding
    # We want to minimize the leftover space, so we prefer bins with smaller remaining capacity
    # After adding, the new remaining capacity would be (bin_capacity - item)
    # We use negative of this to prioritize smaller leftovers
    valid_bins = can_fit
    if np.any(valid_bins):
        new_remaining = bins[valid_bins] - item
        # Prioritize bins with smallest new remaining capacity (i.e., tightest fit)
        priorities[valid_bins] = -new_remaining
    
    return priorities

def priority(item: float, bins: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    target_fraction = 0.5
    remaining_after = bins - item
    valid = remaining_after >= 0
    pri = np.full_like(bins, -np.inf, dtype=float)
    if np.any(valid):
        utilization_after = 1.0 - (remaining_after[valid] / bins[valid])
        pri[valid] = -np.abs(utilization_after - target_fraction)
    return pri

    # Bins that cannot fit the item get very low priority (negative infinity)
    can_fit = remaining >= item
    priorities = np.full_like(bins, -np.inf)
    
    # For bins that can fit the item, prioritize based on remaining capacity after adding
    # We want to maximize the utilization, so we prefer bins with larger remaining capacity after adding
    # After adding, the new remaining capacity would be (bin_capacity - item)
    # We use positive of this to prioritize larger leftovers (i.e., more efficient use of large bins)
    valid_bins = can_fit
    if np.any(valid_bins):
        new_remaining = bins[valid_bins] - item
        # Prioritize bins with largest new remaining capacity (i.e., larger bins used efficiently)
        priorities[valid_bins] = new_remaining
